title: Six-Figure Employees
description:
Report the `name` and `salary` of every employee earning **more than 100000**.

Name the columns `name` and `salary`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > 100000;
hint: A plain WHERE filter. Remember that comparisons against NULL are never true — a NULL salary is not > 100000.

title: Headcount Per Department
description:
Report every department name and how many employees it has. Departments with **no employees** must still appear, with a count of 0.

Name the columns `department` and `employees`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT d.name AS department, COUNT(e.id) AS employees
FROM departments d
LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.dept_id = d.id
GROUP BY d.id, d.name;
hint: COUNT(*) would count the NULL row a LEFT JOIN produces for an empty department. Count a column from the right table instead.

title: Employees Without A Manager
description:
Report the `name` of every employee who has no manager.

Name the column `name`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL;
hint: `manager_id = NULL` is never true. NULL needs its own operator.

title: Distinct Job Titles
description:
Report each distinct job title held by at least one employee.

Name the column `title`. Return the result in any order.
hint: DISTINCT, or an equivalent GROUP BY.

title: Hired Since 2020
description:
Report the `name` and `hire_date` of everyone hired on or after 1 January 2020.

Name the columns `name` and `hire_date`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql: SELECT name, hire_date FROM employees WHERE hire_date >= '2020-01-01';
hint: ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD) compare correctly as plain strings — no date function needed.

title: Department Payroll
description:
Report each department's name and its total salary bill. A department with no employees (or only NULL salaries) must report `0`, not NULL.

Name the columns `department` and `payroll`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT d.name AS department, COALESCE(SUM(e.salary), 0) AS payroll
FROM departments d
LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.dept_id = d.id
GROUP BY d.id, d.name;
hint: SUM over no rows is NULL, not 0. Wrap it in COALESCE or IFNULL.

title: Average Salary, Rounded
description:
Report the company-wide average salary, rounded to 2 decimal places.

Name the column `avg_salary`. The result is exactly one row.
solutionSql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) AS avg_salary FROM employees;
hint: AVG skips NULL salaries automatically — and over an empty table it yields NULL, which is the expected answer there.

title: Names Beginning With A
description:
Report the `name` of every employee whose name begins with the letter `A`.

Name the column `name`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE name LIKE 'A%';
hint: LIKE with a trailing wildcard. In SQLite, LIKE is case-insensitive for ASCII by default.

title: Top Salary In The Company
description:
Report the single highest salary in the company.

Name the column `top_salary`. The result is exactly one row (NULL if there are no employees).
solutionSql: SELECT MAX(salary) AS top_salary FROM employees;
hint: A bare aggregate always returns exactly one row, even with no data — which is why MAX beats ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1 here.

title: How Many Of Each Title
description:
Report each job title and the number of employees holding it, but only for titles held by **two or more** people.

Name the columns `title` and `headcount`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT title, COUNT(*) AS headcount
FROM employees
GROUP BY title
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;
hint: Filtering on an aggregate is HAVING, not WHERE.

title: Departments In Austin
description:
Report the `name` of every department located in Austin.

Name the column `name`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql: SELECT name FROM departments WHERE location = 'Austin';
hint: Straight equality filter on the departments table alone.

title: Salary Range Per Title
description:
For each job title report the lowest and highest salary paid.

Name the columns `title`, `min_salary` and `max_salary`. Return the result in any order.
hint: Two aggregates over the same GROUP BY.
